en: to be embarrassed; to be ashamed

examples.en: I fell in front of everyone and it was embarrassing.

examples.ko: 그런 말을 한 게 지금도 창피스러워요.
examples.en: I am still embarrassed that I said something like that.
I made an embarrassing mistake again.

examples.ko: 시험을 못 본 게 창피스럽지 않아요.
examples.en: I am not ashamed that I did badly on the test.

examples.ko: 창피스럽고 속상해서 아무 말도 못 했어요.
examples.en: I was embarrassed and upset, so I could not say anything.
My face turns red when I am embarrassed.

explain: 비슷한 말로 '창피하다'와 '부끄럽다'가 있어요. '창피하다'는 남이 보는 앞에서 체면이 상할 때, '부끄럽다'는 스스로 느끼는 마음에도 써요. 이 단어는 'ㅂ'이 '워'로 바뀌어서 '창피스러워요'가 돼요.

phrases.en: Cheating on a test is an embarrassing thing.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 앞에서는 '창피스러운'으로 바뀌어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Before a noun it changes to 창피스러운.

phrases.example: 모르는 건 물어보는 게 창피스럽지 않아요.
phrases.en: It's not embarrassing to ask about what you don't know.
phrases.nuance_ko: 부정할 때는 '창피스럽지 않다'라고 해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The negative form is 창피스럽지 않다.

phrases.en: I'm embarrassed because I cried in front of people.
phrases.nuance_ko: '창피스럽다'와 뜻이 같고 일상 대화에서 더 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as 창피스럽다 and more common in everyday speech.

explain_en: Loss of face from a mistake in front of others. Similar words are 'changpihada' and 'bukkeureopda'. 'Changpihada' is for losing face in front of others; 'bukkeureopda' can also describe a feeling you have about yourself. This word changes ㅂ to 워: 'changpiseureowoyo'.

t90.ax: I made an embarrassing mistake again.

examples.en: My little brother sulked because his toy was taken away.

examples.ko: 여자 친구가 토라져서 말을 안 해요.
examples.en: My girlfriend is sulking and won't talk to me.
The child went into the room with a sulky face.

examples.ko: 별것도 아닌 일로 왜 자꾸 토라져요?
examples.en: Why do you keep sulking over nothing?

examples.ko: 친구가 토라진 것 같아서 먼저 사과했어요.
examples.en: My friend seemed upset, so I apologized first.
Don't sulk. Tell me the reason.

explain: 서운하거나 마음이 상해서 말을 안 하거나 표정을 굳히는 모습이에요. 화를 크게 내는 '화나다'와 달리 조용히 삐치는 느낌이고, 가까운 사이에서 많이 써요. 비슷한 '삐치다'는 더 구어체예요.

phrases.en: My younger sibling is sitting with a sulky face.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 앞에서 꾸미는 활용형이고, 삐친 얼굴을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A modifier form describing a sulky face.

phrases.en: My friend is sulking and won't talk.
phrases.nuance_ko: '토라지다'보다 더 구어체예요.
phrases.nuance_en: More colloquial than '토라지다'.

phrases.en: Please don't sulk, it was my fault.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가까운 사람에게 달래듯이 부탁할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to coax someone close to you not to sulk.

explain_en: Feel hurt and withdraw emotionally, not only the lips. It describes going quiet or stiff-faced because you feel hurt or let down. Unlike '화나다', which is open anger, it feels like quietly sulking and is used between close people. The similar '삐치다' is more colloquial.

t90.ax: Don't sulk. Tell me the reason.

en: to be messy; to be untidy; to be disorderly

examples.en: My room is so messy that I can't invite guests.
The top of your desk is really messy.
Clothes are scattered messily across the floor.

examples.ko: 너저분한 짐을 정리하느라 하루가 다 갔어요.
examples.en: I spent the whole day sorting out the cluttered stuff.
Even though I cleaned, the house is still untidy.
Put things back in place so it doesn't get messy.

explain: 물건이 여기저기 흩어져 어수선한 모습에 초점이 있어요. '지저분하다'는 더럽다는 뜻도 있지만, '너저분하다'는 정리가 안 된 느낌이 중심이에요.

phrases.en: I tidied up the messy room today.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 앞에서 꾸며 주는 활용형이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The modifier form placed before a noun.

phrases.en: The desk is messy. I should clear it up.
phrases.nuance_ko: 현재 상태를 말하는 해요체 존댓말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A polite present-tense form describing the current state.

phrases.en: My room isn't very messy.
phrases.nuance_ko: 부정으로 말할 때 쓰는 활용형이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The negative form.

explain_en: The focus is on things lying scattered around in disorder. '지저분하다' can also mean dirty, but '너저분하다' is mainly about things not being tidied up.

examples.ko: 대학교 때 단칸방에서 친구와 같이 살았어요.
examples.en: In college, I lived with a friend in a one-room place.
It's a one-room place, so it's a bit inconvenient when guests come.
I heard my parents started out in a one-room place in Seoul.

examples.ko: 단칸방에 이사 온 첫날 밤은 정말 추웠어요.
examples.en: The first night after moving into the one-room place was really cold.

examples.ko: 그 단칸방은 작아도 햇빛이 잘 들어와요.
examples.en: That one-room place is small, but it gets plenty of sunlight.

examples.ko: 단칸방을 떠나 더 넓은 집으로 옮기고 싶어요.
examples.en: I want to leave this one-room place and move to a bigger home.

explain: 방이 한 칸뿐인 작은 집이에요. 요즘은 '원룸'을 더 많이 쓰고, '단칸방'은 예전 이야기나 어려웠던 살림을 말할 때 자주 나와요. 부엌이나 화장실이 따로 있는지는 상황마다 달라요.

phrases.en: We lived in a one-room home when we were newlyweds.
phrases.nuance_ko: '살다'와 함께 쓰면 어떤 집에 살았는지 자연스럽게 말할 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Pairing it with 'live' is a natural way to say what kind of home someone lived in.
phrases.en_equiv: to live in a one-room home

phrases.en: Our home back then was a one-room place.
phrases.nuance_ko: 예전 살림을 떠올리며 과거형으로 자주 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: It is often used in the past tense when recalling how life used to be.

phrases.en: I live in a small studio now.
phrases.nuance_ko: '단칸방'과 비슷하지만 요즘 집을 말할 때는 '원룸'을 더 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar in meaning, but 'wonrum' is the more common word for homes today.

explain_en: It is a small home with just one room. These days '원룸' is used much more, and '단칸방' often comes up in stories about the past or hard living conditions. Whether it has a separate kitchen or bathroom varies.

examples.en: We tore apart and remodeled the old house into a cafe.
My father took apart and rebuilt the old desk himself.
We have to overhaul the plan from the beginning.

examples.ko: 그 나쁜 버릇을 뜯어고치기가 쉽지 않아요.
examples.en: It isn't easy to completely break that bad habit.
Many people say the system should be overhauled.

examples.ko: 부엌을 뜯어고치는 데 한 달이 걸렸어요.
examples.en: It took a month to completely remodel the kitchen.

explain: 그냥 '고치다'보다 뜯어서 크게 바꾼다는 느낌이 강해요. 집이나 가구 같은 물건뿐 아니라 버릇, 제도, 계획처럼 뿌리부터 바꿀 때도 써요. 작은 수리에는 '고치다'가 더 자연스러워요.

phrases.en: I decided to completely break my habit of sleeping in.
phrases.nuance_ko: 물건뿐 아니라 나쁜 버릇을 뿌리부터 바꿀 때도 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used not only for objects but also for changing a bad habit completely.

phrases.en: We are remodeling this whole room.
phrases.nuance_ko: 해요체 활용으로, 크게 바꾸는 계획이나 습관을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Polite present form, used for big changes in plans or habits.

phrases.en: I fixed the broken chair.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뜯어고치는 것보다 작게 수리할 때 쓰는 더 쉬운 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A simpler word for smaller repairs, less drastic than 뜯어고치다.

explain_en: It feels much bigger than plain '고치다', as if you take something apart and change it greatly. It is used for objects like houses and furniture, and also for changing habits, systems or plans from the root. For small repairs, '고치다' sounds more natural.

t90.ax: We have to overhaul the plan from the beginning.

examples.en: The wind is blowing and the door is rattling.
I replaced the old door with a new one.
The car door got dented, so I took it in for repair.
The door came off, so I have to put it back on.
The child cried after getting a hand caught in the door.
The wardrobe door won't open.

explain: '문'은 열고 닫는 장치 전체를 말하고, '문짝'은 그 문의 판자 부분만 가리켜요. 그래서 '문짝이 떨어지다', '자동차 문짝'처럼 문이 부서지거나 고칠 때 자주 써요. 방 입구의 문을 말할 때는 '문'이라고 해요.

phrases.en: The door panel fell off, so I have to fix it.
phrases.nuance_ko: 문이 망가졌을 때 쓰는 대표적인 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A typical phrase for when a door is broken.

phrases.en: There is a scratch on the car door.
phrases.nuance_ko: 자동차의 문 부분을 말할 때 '문짝'을 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: '문짝' is often used for the door part of a car.

phrases.en: The wardrobe door doesn't close well.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가구의 열고 닫는 판을 말할 때도 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Also used for the panel that opens and closes on furniture.

explain_en: '문' refers to the whole door setup, while '문짝' points to the panel itself. So it is common when a door breaks or is repaired, as in '문짝이 떨어지다' and '자동차 문짝'. For the door of a room, just say '문'.

dis.h: the door panel itself, as a part

p.n: 문짝 stresses the panel part that came off; 문 only says the door.

examples.en: The car's bumper got dented.
I scratched the bumper while parking.
How much is the repair for the front bumper?
The bumper color is different from the car.
Please don't put stickers on the bumper.
The car behind bumped me lightly with its bumper.

explain: 차의 앞과 뒤 끝에 있는 부분이라 '앞 범퍼', '뒤 범퍼'로 말해요. 사고가 나면 '범퍼가 나갔다', '범퍼가 찌그러졌다'라고 하고, 놀이공원에서 부딪치며 타는 차는 '범퍼카'예요.

phrases.en: The front bumper is a little cracked.
phrases.nuance_ko: 차의 앞쪽 범퍼를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to the bumper at the front of the car.

phrases.en: I put a sticker on the rear bumper.
phrases.nuance_ko: 차의 뒤쪽 범퍼를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to the bumper at the back of the car.

phrases.en: There was an accident and the bumper got wrecked.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사고로 범퍼가 크게 망가졌다는 말투예요.
phrases.nuance_en: A casual way to say the bumper was badly damaged in a crash.

explain_en: It sits at the front and back ends of a car, so you say 앞 범퍼 and 뒤 범퍼. After an accident people say '범퍼가 찌그러졌다' (the bumper is dented), and the bumping ride at an amusement park is 범퍼카.

examples.en: The shower at my house has weak water pressure.
The upper floors have low water pressure, which is inconvenient.

examples.ko: 잠수부는 깊이 들어갈수록 수압을 많이 받아요.
examples.en: The deeper a diver goes, the more water pressure they feel.
The hose almost burst because of the water pressure.

examples.ko: 수도꼭지 수압을 조절하는 방법을 알려 주세요.
examples.en: Please tell me how to adjust the faucet's water pressure.

examples.ko: 수압이 너무 세면 물이 사방으로 튀어요.
examples.en: If the water pressure is too strong, water splashes everywhere.

explain: '수압이 세다', '수압이 약하다'처럼 샤워기나 수도꼭지 이야기에 가장 많이 써요. 깊은 바닷속에서 몸이 받는 압력도 수압이에요.

phrases.example: 이 수도는 수압이 세서 물이 튀어요.
phrases.en: This tap has strong water pressure, so the water splashes.
phrases.nuance_ko: 물이 세게 나올 때 일상에서 가장 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common daily phrase when water comes out hard.

phrases.en: The deeper you go, the higher the water pressure gets.
phrases.nuance_ko: 바닷속처럼 깊은 물에서 받는 압력을 말할 때도 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Also used for the pressure felt deep underwater.

phrases.en: You can adjust the shower's water pressure.
phrases.nuance_ko: 기계나 수도꼭지로 세기를 바꾼다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means changing the strength using a device or tap.

explain_en: The common phrases are 수압이 세다 and 수압이 약하다, mostly about showers and faucets. The pressure on your body deep underwater is also 수압.

examples.en: My phone's screen cracked.
I was surprised at how expensive the screen repair was.
I put on a new screen protector.

examples.ko: 햇빛 때문에 액정이 잘 안 보여요.
examples.en: I can't see the screen well because of the sunlight.
This monitor has a sharp screen.
There are lots of fingerprints on the screen.

explain: 액정은 원래 액정 디스플레이(LCD)의 줄임말이지만, 한국에서는 휴대폰이나 TV의 화면 부분을 두루 가리키는 말로 써요. 휴대폰 화면이 깨졌을 때 '액정이 나갔다', '액정이 깨졌다'고도 말해요. 수리점에서는 '액정 교체'라는 말을 들을 수 있어요.

phrases.example: 액정이 나가서 화면이 하나도 안 보여요.
phrases.en: The screen went out, so I can't see anything on the display.
phrases.nuance_ko: 화면이 깨지지 않아도 고장 나서 안 나올 때 일상에서 많이 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A casual way to say the screen has broken down and no longer works.

phrases.example: 새 휴대폰은 액정 화면이 커서 좋아요.
phrases.en: I like the new phone because its screen is big.
phrases.nuance_ko: 액정과 화면을 함께 붙여 화면 부분을 분명하게 말하는 쓰임이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Putting the two words together to clearly refer to the display part.

phrases.en: I put a protective film on the screen.
phrases.nuance_ko: 깨지거나 긁히지 않게 화면에 붙이는 얇은 막을 말할 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Commonly used for the thin film stuck on a screen to prevent cracks and scratches.

explain_en: Aekjeong is originally short for liquid-crystal display, but in Korea it commonly means the screen part of a phone or TV. When a phone screen breaks, people also say 액정이 나갔다 or 액정이 깨졌다. At repair shops you may hear 액정 교체.

examples.en: The wind was strong, so the umbrella rib broke.

examples.ko: 우산살 하나가 휘어서 잘 안 펴져요.
examples.en: One rib is bent, so the umbrella doesn't open well.
My finger got caught in the umbrella ribs and it hurt.
It's a new umbrella, but the ribs are already bent.

examples.ko: 우산살을 고쳐 주는 가게를 찾고 있어요.
examples.en: I'm looking for a shop that repairs umbrella ribs.

examples.ko: 이 우산은 우산살이 가늘어서 센 바람에 약해요.
examples.en: This umbrella has thin ribs, so it is weak against strong wind.

explain: 우산의 천을 받치는 가는 뼈대예요. 손잡이 쪽 긴 막대는 '우산대'라고 해서 구분해요.

phrases.en: The umbrella rib broke, so I bought a new umbrella.
phrases.nuance_ko: 바람이 센 날 우산이 망가졌을 때 가장 자주 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common collocation for an umbrella breaking on a windy day.

phrases.en: The umbrella ribs bent because of the wind.
phrases.nuance_ko: '부러지다'보다 약하게, 구부러진 상태를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Milder than 부러지다; it describes ribs that are bent rather than broken.

phrases.en: My father fixed the umbrella ribs for me.
phrases.nuance_ko: 망가진 우산을 수리하는 상황에서 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when repairing a damaged umbrella.

explain_en: These are the thin frame bars that hold up the umbrella fabric. The long shaft on the handle side is called '우산대', so the two are different parts.

examples.ko: 아기가 젖병을 잡고 혼자 우유를 먹어요.
examples.en: The baby holds the bottle and drinks milk by himself.
Every night I mix formula in the bottle and feed the baby.

examples.ko: 여행 갈 때 젖병도 꼭 챙기세요.
examples.en: Be sure to pack the baby bottle when you travel.
I needed a new baby bottle, so I went to the mart.

examples.ko: 아기 젖병은 끓는 물 소독이 필요해요.
examples.en: Baby bottles need to be sterilized in boiling water.

examples.ko: 젖병 꼭지가 너무 커서 아기가 힘들어해요.
examples.en: The bottle nipple is too big, so the baby has a hard time.

explain: 아기에게 우유나 분유를 먹이는 병이에요. '젖병을 물리다'는 아기에게 젖병을 입에 물려 먹인다는 말이고, '젖병을 떼다'는 아기가 젖병 쓰는 것을 끝낸다는 말이에요. 병의 끝에 붙은 부분은 '젖꼭지'라고 해요.

phrases.en: The baby was crying, so I gave it the bottle.
phrases.nuance_ko: 아기 입에 젖병을 물려 먹이는 동작을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: It describes putting the bottle in the baby's mouth to feed it.
phrases.en_equiv: to give a baby a bottle

phrases.example: 우리 아이는 두 살에 젖병을 뗐어요.
phrases.en: Our child gave up the bottle at age two.
phrases.nuance_ko: 아기가 젖병 쓰는 것을 끝낸다는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: It means a baby stops using the bottle.

phrases.example: 분유를 타기 전에 젖병을 깨끗이 씻어요.
phrases.en: I wash the baby bottle clean before mixing the formula.
phrases.nuance_ko: 육아에서 매일 하는 일이라서 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: It is a daily childcare chore, so the phrase is common.

explain_en: It is the bottle used to feed a baby milk or formula. '젖병을 물리다' means to put the bottle in the baby's mouth to feed, and '젖병을 떼다' means the baby stops using bottles. The nipple part on the bottle is called '젖꼭지'.

examples.en: My father's car still has a cassette player.
My grandmother listens to old songs on a cassette player.
I don't know where the cassette tape went.

examples.ko: 중학교 때 카세트로 영어 듣기를 연습했어요.
examples.en: In middle school, I practiced English listening with a cassette player.

examples.ko: 이 카세트는 고장 나서 소리가 안 나요.
examples.en: This cassette player is broken and makes no sound.
These days, shops that sell cassettes are rare.

explain: '카세트 테이프'라고 해서 테이프 자체를 말하기도 하고, 테이프를 트는 기계를 말하기도 해요. 요즘은 스마트폰으로 음악을 들어서 옛날 이야기를 할 때 많이 나와요. 기계는 '카세트 플레이어'라고도 해요.

phrases.en: I found an old cassette tape in the drawer.
phrases.nuance_ko: 음악이나 소리를 담은 테이프 자체를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to the tape itself that holds the music or sound.

phrases.en: My father listens to music on a cassette player.
phrases.nuance_ko: 테이프를 트는 기계를 분명히 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Makes it clear you mean the machine that plays the tape.

phrases.en: I played a cassette in the car and listened to songs.
phrases.nuance_ko: 테이프로 음악을 재생할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when playing music from a tape.

explain_en: It can mean the tape itself, called 카세트 테이프, or the machine that plays it. Since people now listen to music on smartphones, it comes up mostly when talking about the past. The machine can also be called 카세트 플레이어.

examples.ko: 마당에 오래된 펌프 한 대가 있어요.
examples.en: There is an old pump in the yard.
I pumped the water up with a pump.

examples.ko: 자전거 바퀴에 바람을 넣으려고 펌프를 샀어요.
examples.en: I bought a pump to put air in the bicycle tire.

examples.ko: 펌프가 고장 나서 물이 안 나와요.
examples.en: The pump is broken, so no water comes out.
A pump can also be operated by hand.
A strange noise comes from this pump.

explain: 물에는 '물 펌프', 자전거에는 '공기 펌프'처럼 앞에 말을 붙여서 구분해요. 펌프를 움직이는 일은 '펌프질'이라고 하고, '펌프질하다'로 써요.

phrases.en: The country house has a water pump.
phrases.nuance_ko: 물을 끌어 올리는 펌프를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for a pump that draws up water.

phrases.example: 자전거 바퀴에 공기 펌프로 바람을 넣어요.
phrases.en: I pump air into the bicycle tire with an air pump.
phrases.nuance_ko: 바람을 넣는 펌프를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for a pump that fills things with air.

phrases.en: The child pumped hard and water came out.
phrases.nuance_ko: 펌프를 움직이는 동작을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes the action of working a pump.

explain_en: You add a word in front to tell kinds apart, like '물 펌프' (water pump) and '공기 펌프' (air pump). Operating a pump is '펌프질', used as '펌프질하다'.
